text_plugin_synopsis: A multi-session terminal for AutoJs6 and its scripts, running the system shell in a pty with background sessions, a key bar and Node.js commands
p_languages_all_supported_for_readme: The current README.md supports the following languages
p_introduction_what: 3-Shell Terminal takes over the built-in terminal of AutoJs6: the "Terminal" switch of the home drawer, "Open in terminal" in the file manager directory menu and the project toolbar, and the script-side global object `terminal` for opening, driving and observing terminal sessions. Every session is a system shell (`/system/bin/sh`) running in a pty that keeps running in the background after the screen is left.
p_introduction_how: AutoJs6 discovers the plugin through its Binder service, opens the terminal screen with an explicit Intent, and uses the Binder to read the session count, close all sessions or drive script sessions; session output flows back to scripts through a pipe. When the Node.js Runtime plugin is installed, the terminal reads its manifest contract directly, verifies the signature and the launcher, and provides node / npm / npx / corepack / yarn / pnpm.
p_status: Version 1.2.0 adds terminal colors and fonts, command completion notices and trust for third-party Node.js signers to the standalone terminal, background sessions, interactive script APIs and settings. Complete script APIs require AutoJs6 6.8.0 build 5315 or later; build 5304 is the base plugin-protocol requirement, and the plugin's file manager directory menu entry requires build 5320. Android 7.0 or later is supported.
p_features_intro: The plugin provides the following capabilities
features: Multiple sessions: create, switch, close and a session manager; a foreground service keeps sessions running after the screen is left, and its notification shows the current directory and the session count with a "Close sessions" action.

Terminal screen: a two-row key bar (Esc / Tab / Ctrl / arrows / common symbols), native text selection with Copy / Select all, transcript copy and share, text size, paste and clear; four terminal color schemes (follow the appearance / dark / light / tinted by the theme color) and the terminal font (system monospace or the built-in JetBrains Mono without ligatures).

Command editor: menu and IME pastes containing multiple lines or more than 80 characters open a complete, wrapping editor. Paste into the current terminal or run in a new session in the current directory with the command and exit code shown (16 KiB command limit). New sessions do not inherit temporary variables or an interactive su login; include su in commands that need Root. Submitted text is kept only in session memory and can be viewed or copied from the text actions menu.

Node.js toolchain: with the Node.js Runtime plugin (1.5.0+) installed, node / npm / npx / corepack / yarn / pnpm become available, together with the npm registry and "ignore install scripts" settings and the package menu (npm init / install / run script and more).

AutoJs6 entries: the home drawer switch (session count, close all), "Open in terminal" in the file manager directory menu and the project toolbar. Since AutoJs6 build 5320 the directory menu item comes from the plugin through the Explorer Action protocol, and AutoJs6 passes only the path of the selected directory. From AutoJs6 6.8.1 this item is in the submenu `3-Shell Terminal`.

Script API `terminal` (alias `$terminal`): session management, visible execution (`exec`, `npm.run`) and a session object with `output` / `exit` events, `write` and `waitFor`; every failure is a `TerminalError` with a stable `code`.

Command completion notices: when a command without an interactive shell (for example a script's `exec` with `keepOpen: false`) ends by itself, a notice opens the end of its output to copy, share or reopen a terminal in its directory; the notice names only the session and directory, never the command or output, and can be turned off in the settings.

Standalone app: the launcher icon opens the terminal directly; a settings page (appearance following AutoJs6, text size, terminal colors and font, npm registry, Node.js integration, trusted Node.js signers, command completion notices, all files access, clear terminal data), About and the release history.
usage_steps: Install the plugin APK matching the device ABI (or the universal APK) from [Releases]({{ repo_url }}/releases) on a device with AutoJs6 build {{ required_host_version_code }} ({{ required_host_version_name }}) or later.
Open the AutoJs6 plugin center, confirm that `3-Shell Terminal` is recognized, and enable it.

Turn on "Terminal" in the AutoJs6 home drawer, choose "Open in terminal" on a directory in the file manager, or call `terminal.open(...)` from a script. Grant "All files access" when the plugin asks for it to enter directories under shared storage such as `/sdcard`.
p_node_intro: How the terminal obtains node / npm and what the limits are
node_points: Requires the Node.js Runtime plugin 1.5.0 or later; the plugin reads its manifest contract, verifies the signature, the launcher and the npm / corepack archive, and links the commands into `PATH` whenever a session starts. Without the plugin, or when verification fails, the terminal stays usable without these commands.

Android prevents execution of app-written files. npm disables bin links by default, so `node_modules/.bin/*` and `npx <package>` cannot directly run package entry points. Use `node node_modules/<package>/<entry>.js`. Native executables bundled in npm packages fail with `EACCES`, and native addons (`.node`) cannot be loaded.

corepack defaults to its bundled pnpm 11.x and Yarn 1.x (`COREPACK_DEFAULT_TO_LATEST=0`) and downloads an explicitly named version on request; the npm registry can be switched to npmmirror or a custom https URL in the settings.
p_quick_start_intro: A script that opens the script directory, installs dependencies visibly and waits for the result, and drives an interactive command (available from roadmap P4 on)
p_compatibility_intro: Platform facts that shape what the plugin can do
compatibility_points: Android 7.0 (API 24) and later; APKs for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 and x86 plus a universal APK, with native libraries aligned to 16 KB pages; the host build and the plugin are verified together on the device matrix listed in [ROADMAP.md]({{ roadmap_url }}).
Terminal processes run under the plugin's own uid and permissions and do not inherit the permissions of AutoJs6; use the script `shell()` API for commands that need AutoJs6 permissions.
Sessions live as long as the plugin process; after the system ends the process they cannot be restored, which the foreground service and its notification make unlikely.
faq_items: **Why does `cd /sdcard/Scripts` fail?** The plugin needs its own storage grant. Open the plugin settings or follow the terminal banner to grant "All files access" (Android 11+), or the storage permission on older systems.

**Can the terminal open a `content://` directory (for example one granted through the system file picker)?** No. A shell can only enter real file system paths, while a `content://` address is reachable only through its content provider. The script API refuses such addresses; other entries return to the home directory with a notice. For shared storage use a path such as `/sdcard/...` and grant all files access.

**Why is there no node command?** Install the Node.js Runtime plugin (1.5.0+) from the AutoJs6 plugin center; the "environment probe" in the plugin settings shows the exact reason (missing, too old, untrusted signature or launcher not executable). For an untrusted signer the probe lists its SHA-256; after you confirm the trust, new sessions can use its commands.

**Can the system stop background sessions?** Yes. Sessions cannot be restored after the plugin process is terminated. On HyperOS, MIUI and other restricted systems, allow notifications and background activity in Android settings; opening the terminal retries foreground protection when permitted. Leaving the screen normally keeps sessions running, but a foreground service cannot override system restrictions.
security_points: The Binder service and the screen entry are protected by the `org.autojs.permission.PLUGIN` signature permission and verify the caller signature, so only AutoJs6 can reach them; the launcher entry only opens the terminal and accepts no external command.
The storage permission ("All files access" on Android 11+) is only used to enter the directories you choose; the terminal never scans or uploads files.

The `INTERNET` permission is used by the commands you run in the shell (for example `npm install`) and by the manual release check against this plugin's fixed GitHub Releases API; the plugin itself never goes online in the background.

The launcher of the Node.js Runtime plugin is executed only when its signature is the official one, matches this plugin, or was confirmed by you after reviewing its SHA-256 on the environment probe screen (revocable in the settings); the plugin does not log session input or output and excludes its private storage from backups.
p_security_permission: Only obtain the plugin from the official [Releases]({{ repo_url }}/releases) page or the AutoJs6 plugin center. Packages from unknown sources may fail host verification or carry risks even when the version number looks identical.
p_plugin_interface: The following information targets AutoJs6 host and plugin developers; the host uses these identifiers to discover the plugin and negotiate compatibility
p_contract_service: `ThreeShellTerminalPluginService` answers `{{ plugin_service_action }}` (category `{{ plugin_service_category }}`) and implements the host terminal-api contract `{{ plugin_aidl_interface }}` from roadmap P2 on. `ThreeShellTerminalPluginInfoService` answers `{{ plugin_info_action }}` with PluginInfo. `WakeActivity` lets the host activate the plugin; the terminal screen is opened through `org.autojs.plugin.TERMINAL_OPEN`. `ThreeShellTerminalExplorerActionService` responds to `org.autojs.plugin.EXPLORER_ACTION` (Explorer Action protocol v23) with the single-directory "Open in terminal" action, which `ThreeShellTerminalExplorerActivity` executes.
p_roadmap: The plugin's plans and progress are maintained as a checkable list in ROADMAP.md, organized by phase with acceptance criteria and evidence levels. Unchecked items express intent rather than current capabilities; discussion via Issues is welcome.
p_build_intro: This section targets developers who want to build the plugin from source; regular users can simply install the prebuilt APK from the Releases page.
p_build_test: Run JVM unit tests and build the instrumentation test APK
p_build_digest: Collect the release artifact and append the version and CRC32 digest to its file name
p_build_docs_check: Verify that the multilingual documentation sources and generated artifacts are in sync (also enforced by CI)
p_build_requirements: Building requires JDK 21 or later and Android SDK 37; Gradle and plugin versions are managed centrally by `version.properties` and `io.github.supermonster003.autojs6-platform-versions`.
p_resource_layout: The language JSON files under `.readme/` and `.changelog/` are the single source for the README, the plugin-center instructions, and the changelog. Always edit those JSON sources and rerun `py .python/generate_markdown.py`; generated README, `plugin_instruction.md`, and changelog artifacts are never edited by hand. Run `py .python/generate_markdown.py --check` to verify all generated artifacts.

instruction_p_what: 3-Shell Terminal is an interactive terminal on your phone: it runs the system `/system/bin/sh` in a pty, keeps several sessions open at once, and keeps them running in the background after you leave the screen. With the Node.js Runtime plugin installed, commands such as node and npm are available too. The "Terminal" entry in AutoJs6 and the `terminal` object in scripts are both provided by this plugin.
instruction_start_steps: Tap "Terminal" in the AutoJs6 home drawer, or choose "Open in terminal" from a folder menu in the file manager; you can also tap the 3-Shell Terminal icon on the home screen.
Type a command and press Enter to run it. The extra keys bar at the bottom of the screen provides Esc, Tab, Ctrl, arrow keys and common symbols.
Create, switch or close sessions from the "Sessions" menu in the toolbar. Sessions keep running after you leave the screen; tap the notification to open "Terminal manager".
Before entering shared storage folders such as `/sdcard`, tap "Grant" when the terminal prompts you, or turn on "All files access" in the settings.
instruction_features: **Multiple sessions**: create, switch and close sessions; "Terminal manager" lists them all. A foreground service keeps sessions running in the background, and the notification shows the current folder and the session count.
**Terminal screen**: extra keys bar, text selection and copy, "Share transcript", and pinch to zoom the text; the settings offer 4 schemes under "Terminal colors" and 2 choices under "Terminal font".
**Command editor**: when you paste a long or multi-line command, the full text is shown first; you can paste it into the current session, or run it in a new session and see the exit code.

**Node.js toolchain**: with the Node.js Runtime plugin installed, node, npm, npx and corepack (yarn / pnpm) are available. In the settings you can pick the "npm registry" or turn on "Ignore npm lifecycle scripts".

**Command completion notifications**: when a command that a script ran without keeping an interactive shell finishes, a notification is posted; tap it to see the end of the output. You can turn off "Command completion notifications" in the settings.

**Separate settings**: language, night mode and theme color follow AutoJs6 by default and can also be set separately; the launcher icon comes in 4 styles. When AutoJs6 supports it, the settings page menu offers "Open general settings".
instruction_p_script: Scripts use the global object `terminal` (alias `$terminal`) to create sessions, run commands, write input and listen to output:
instruction_script_notes: By default, `exec` keeps an interactive shell after the command finishes; to wait for the exit code, set both `keepOpen: false` and `wait: true`.
Synchronous methods block the script thread and cannot be called on the UI thread; most methods also have an `Async` form that returns a Promise.
Sessions keep running after the script exits; call `session.close()` when you no longer need them. A failed operation throws a `TerminalError` with a `code`.
For all options and events, see [AutoJs6 docs > Terminal]({{ docs_terminal_url }}).
instruction_requirements: Android {{ min_android_version }} or later, and AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }} or later.
Commands such as node and npm need the [Node.js Runtime]({{ nodejs_plugin_url }}) plugin 1.5.0 or later.

Entering shared storage folders needs "All files access" (Android 11 and later) or the storage permission; the notification permission is used for session notifications and command completion notifications.
Commands run with this plugin's own identity and permissions, not those of AutoJs6; for commands that need the permissions of AutoJs6, use `shell()` in a script instead.

instruction_faq.a: This plugin needs its own storage access. Tap "Grant" when the terminal prompts you, or turn on "All files access" in the settings; on Android 10 and earlier, granting the storage permission is enough. A `content://` address is not a file path and cannot be entered.

instruction_faq.q: The node command is not found
instruction_faq.a: Make sure the Node.js Runtime plugin is installed and "Node.js integration" is on in the settings, then open "Node.js launcher check" to see why. If the plugin is not signed with the official signature, that page shows the SHA-256 of its signature; once you confirm you trust it, new sessions can use it.

instruction_faq.q: Background sessions are ended by the system
instruction_faq.a: Once the system ends the plugin process, its sessions cannot be restored. Systems such as HyperOS and MIUI may restrict background activity; in the system settings, allow 3-Shell Terminal to post notifications and run in the background.

instruction_p_more: For details on the extra keys, the script interface and permissions, see the [project page]({{ repo_url }}).
